provenance.paper_title: HiKEY: Hierarchical Multimodal Retrieval for Open-Domain Document Question Answering

representation_paths.memory_component: Section-level cards holding text, table and image units as first-class retrieval units over the document corpus

evidence.section: Full paper (arXiv HTML v1): Sec. 3.1 Offline hierarchy-aware graph and index construction; Sec. 3.2 Type-Specific Unit Score
evidence.paraphrase: Each document is decomposed into Doc_cards (title plus section paths, used for global routing) and Sec_cards, whose entries are multimodal units typed as Text, Table or Image. Tables and figures are retained as first-class retrieval units rather than being replaced by captions, and the retrieved visual units are delivered to the reader, so the perceptual source is directly available downstream. Stage-1 routing ranks Doc_cards with a hybrid lexical-plus-dense score; Stage-2 globally ranks constituent Sec_cards and their units with a type-specific unit score combining text-semantic and dense visual-semantic signals.

representation_paths.memory_component: Document Hierarchical Parsing tree linking blocks as parent-child nodes with ancestor section paths, traversed to attach Upper Context to caption-less visual units

evidence.section: Full paper (arXiv HTML v1): Sec. 3.1 Document Hierarchical Parsing and Contextual Enrichment via Graph Traversal
evidence.paraphrase: Documents are reconstructed into a hierarchical tree T(d) whose blocks are nodes connected by parent-child tree edges, with each unit assigned an ancestor section path such as Title > Section 5 > 5.3. For visual units lacking captions, HiKEY traverses the tree upward to the logically preceding textual node and attaches it as Upper Context, so the tree structure is itself operative at retrieval time and links every enriched unit back to its originating document block.

derived.hybrid_relation: The retained multimodal unit store and the hierarchy tree are deliberately linked: tree traversal supplies Upper Context that enriches the stored visual units, and the two-stage scorer consumes the hierarchical routing signal and the unit-level multimodal signal jointly.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (arXiv HTML v1, Sec. 3.1-3.2, Limitations, Appendix D.1): assigned T1. The paper states that Document Hierarchical Parsing and indexing are an offline, one-time cost; at query time HiKEY runs a fixed coarse-to-fine routing and ranking procedure and never writes back to, reorganizes, or prunes the index. No deployment feedback touches any write, maintenance, or retrieval policy.

Scope: this is a corpus-side multimodal retrieval memory rather than agent experience memory, retained on the same basis as the existing VisRAG and MARDoc records in this corpus. Non-text participation is genuine: image and table units are stored, scored with dense visual-semantic signals, and returned as evidence.
